newsitem.title: INDIA: SBI to observe strike in New Delhi June 19.
newsitem.headline: SBI to observe strike in New Delhi June 19.

text.p: Officers of the State Bank of India's 200 branches in the Indian capital will observe a one-day strike on June 19 to protest against suspension of their colleagues in Bombay, bank officials said on Tuesday.
"All dealing transactions will be suspended," M.V. Rao, vice president of SBI Officers Association (Delhi circle), told Reuters. SBI is the country's largest public sector chain of commercial banks.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted an SBI statement as saying that the strike would be observed to protest the suspension of three SBI officials in Bombay on charges of failure to follow procedures in handling accounts of CRB Capital Markets, a finance company now facing liquidation proceedings.
PTI quoted the statement as saying four other officials were suspended in connection with a different case. "The suspensions were baseless and no ground rules were followed," Rao said.
On Tuesday talks between agitating SBI officers and the management failed as a strike entered its fifth day in Bombay.
The strike, which began at the Bombay head office, has now spread to the western states of Maharashtra (of which Bombay is the capital) and Goa.
SBI's board is meeting in Calcutta on June 19 to finalise accounts for the year ended March 31, 1997.
